findings.what_viewer_sees: The Explorer has ridden Australia into the middle of the Pacific. At 5:25.87 he jumps about 130 px in one frame, from Australia's north coast to its south-east interior. Asia blinks onto a third of the globe in the same frame. The shot was completely still for the frames before, so the hiccup is obvious just before "Yes, even Asia".
findings.evidence: Full-res crops 9774-9777: the hero centre moves from about (934,374) to (1016,474) between 9775 and 9776. Quarter-res changed-pixel count is 0-2 for 9768-9775 and 3856 at 9776. The raw chunk c_00021 shows the same jump at local frame 326, which is global 9776. Code time tAusA = tm.drop + 3.8 = 325.86, and 9776 is the first frame with t >= tAusA.
findings.likely_cause: heroAt is taken from Australia's flying centroid only while t < d.t1 (line 940). From tAusA on, the else branch (line 947) places him at rotAB(pac, heroEnd, 0.15 + 0.85*k2), and k2 stays 0 until tAsiaA + 0.05. That point is already 15% (about 12 degrees) of the way to heroEnd, so his position snaps the moment Australia lands.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the hand-off continuous. At line 947 use `const off = 0.15 * prog(t, tAusA, tAusA + 0.5, E.inOut); const R = L.rotAB(pac, heroEnd, off + (1 - off) * k2);`, or drop the 0.15 and use k2 alone. He then starts exactly at pac, where Australia delivered him, and slides out as Australia melts. Re-render chunk 21 (frames 9450-9899).

findings.what_viewer_sees: Over "The Pacific alone could swallow every continent", each continent should fly over the horizon into the Pacific. Instead each one appears in a single frame at the rim, fully opaque and already half on the visible side. Africa (5:23.97) and Asia (5:25.87) are the worst: a big orange shape with white borders blinks onto the globe. North America (5:22.27) pops in as a thick crescent on the limb.
findings.evidence: Quarter-res orange-fill pixel counts: f9667 -> 9668 goes from 0 to 839 px (North America). f9718 -> 9719 adds 1869 px against about 100-200 px per frame around it (Africa). f9703 -> 9704 adds 57 px of white outline (Europe). At f9775 -> 9776, 3856 px change after a static stretch (Asia). Seen in frame runs 9656-9679, 9680-9703, 9704-9727 and 9768-9783.
findings.likely_cause: The drop loop skips a continent entirely while its rotated centroid is behind the globe (`if (!pj.xyz(cc...)[2]) continue;`). globePath already clamps hidden vertices to the limb, so on the frame the centroid crosses the horizon, half the continent is drawn at full alpha at once.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the centroid `continue` and fade by how far the centroid is over the horizon instead. For example, add facing(x,y,z) to L.projector (returning dot(v, camDir) - h) and multiply the alpha at line 937 by smooth(-0.35, 0.05, facing); skip only when that is 0. The clamped path then rises over the limb. Compute Australia's heroAt regardless of visibility. Re-render chunk 21.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The "Ocean on top / land at the bottom / land avoiding land" montage is meant to have a brief white flash at each cut. Instead, from the cut to the south disc (5:29.37) the whole frame sits under a constant 18% white veil. The south disc's background turns grey, and the antipode map at 5:31 looks milky, much flatter than the same map at 4:38. At the cut to the water globe (5:32.23-5:32.30) the veil drains over three frames, which reads as a darkening flash.
findings.evidence: Corner RGB: north disc 9876-9880 is (0, 0.3, 7). South disc 9881-9925 is a constant (16, 26, 35). EE map 9926-9966 is (19-30, 29-49, 33-54). Water tile: 9967 (15, 26, 34), 9968 (4, 15, 24), 9969 (0, 1, 9), 9970 (0, 0.3, 7). The montage EE map has a frame mean of 74 against 43 for the same image at 8400.
findings.likely_cause: `fl = Math.max(1 - prog(t, tMont2, ..), 1 - prog(t, tMont3, ..), 1 - prog(t, tMont4, ..))`. For any t before a later cut, `1 - prog(t, tCut, ...)` is 1, so fl stays 1 from tMont2 until tMont4 + 0.12 instead of decaying after each cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Count only cuts already passed: `const fl = Math.max(0, ...[tMont2, tMont3, tMont4].map(c => t >= c ? 1 - prog(t, c, c + 0.12, E.lin) : 0));`. Re-render the tail of chunk 21 (frames 9881-9899) and chunk 22 (9900-10349).

findings.frames: 9967-10036 (montage water globe, full-res 10010); also the 2x3 grid 9220-9362
findings.what_viewer_sees: The "water half" globe in the montage sits on a hard-edged black square that slowly tilts to about 3 degrees, so it looks like a pasted screenshot on the navy background. It is also visibly soft compared with every other globe in the film. The same black squares sit behind the six globes in the "no half is mostly land" grid, where they read as unbordered dark cards.
findings.evidence: In full-res frame 10010 a black square spans roughly (510-1410, 98-1000), rotated, with blurred coastlines and atmosphere rim. The same is visible in 10034-10036 and in grid frames 9225-9310.
findings.likely_cause: renderTile renders a full opaque globe frame (the background shader writes alpha 1) and copies a square crop into a 420x420 canvas. The montage draws that tile at 820-900 px (about a 2x upscale) with ctx.rotate(0.05*k), and the grid draws it at 340 px.
findings.suggested_fix: Mask the tile to the disc when copying. After the drawImage at line 848, set tc.globalCompositeOperation = 'destination-in' and fill a radial-gradient circle: opaque out to the disc radius plus an atmosphere margin, transparent beyond. Also render the montage tile larger (for example 900x900), or draw that globe live with api.drawGlobe instead of a cached tile. Re-render chunks 20 and 22.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The JUICE CHECK "?" stamp flies from top-left toward the globe. On the landing frame it skips the last stretch of its path, nearly vanishes (about 10% opacity) and doubles in size, then reappears solid and slams down. At speed this is a one-frame blink or stutter inside the slam.
findings.evidence: Frames 10578-10582: at 10579 the small stamp is at about (1037, 442) and fully opaque. At 10580 a faint ghost about twice the size sits at about (1306, 557). At 10581 the stamp is big and solid, then settles by 10586.
findings.likely_cause: When `landed` flips (t >= tm.checks - pre), juiceStamp restarts with lt = 0, and its alpha clamp(p*3) is about 0.1 on that frame. The flight uses E.in, so on its last frame it has covered only about 71% of the path.
findings.suggested_fix: In ch2_lib.js:155 add an opt-out: `ctx.globalAlpha *= (o.fadeIn === false ? 1 : clamp(p * 3)) * (o.alpha ?? 1)`, and pass `fadeIn: !landed` at ch2.js:1065. End the flight on the frame before the slam, e.g. `prog(t, tm.checks - 0.35, tm.checks - pre - 1/30, E.in)`, so the stamp reaches gc before landing. Re-render chunk 23.

findings.what_viewer_sees: As the tetrahedron rotates, its fourth corner comes round the globe's upper-left limb. Its glowing dot (about a 60 px glow) appears in one frame at full brightness, while everything else in the 1875 shot eases.
findings.evidence: Crop of frames 10292-10299 at the upper-left limb: no glow at 10296, full glow at 10297. The bright-pixel count goes from 934 to 1251 in one frame.
findings.likely_cause: Corner alpha uses a binary ray-sphere occlusion test. An occluded corner gets 0.35*xr, which is about 0 before the x-ray ramps up; a visible one gets 1. The corner therefore jumps from 0 to 1 on the frame it clears the limb, and any later limb crossing is a 0.35-to-1 step.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a soft occlusion factor: `const dPerp = Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, cq + R*R - bq*bq)); const vis = (-bq < Ld) ? smooth(R*0.97, R*1.08, dPerp) : 1; const a = lerp(0.35*xr, 1, vis) * prog(t, tm.g1875 - pre, tm.g1875 + 0.6);`. The corner then fades in over the last few degrees before it clears the limb. Re-render chunk 22.

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the hard cut to the drip globe, "WHY DO THE CONTINENTS" appears all at once and already 65-100% formed. Only "POINT SOUTH?" rise in. The word-by-word rise used by the other headlines is lost for most of this one, so the headline pops.
findings.evidence: Frame 10037, the first frame of the scene, shows four words at near-full opacity. POINT arrives at 10038 and SOUTH? at 10040.
findings.likely_cause: The headline clock starts at tm.lop - 0.35 (334.29), but the scene starts at cDrip = tm.lop - 0.1 (334.54). So 0.25 s of the 0.07 s-per-word stagger has already elapsed on the first frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the headline with the scene: `t - (cDrip + 0.03)` with `tOut: cTet - cDrip - 0.23`, which keeps the same absolute fade-out. Re-render chunk 22.

findings.what_viewer_sees: When the lit squares slide into the bottom rows ("sprinkled at random"), the cells they leave behind stay empty. Both 10x10 grids look moth-eaten, with a ghost of the random pattern, for the 2 s the chart is held, and the 29-vs-13 comparison reads less cleanly.
findings.evidence: Frames 8646-8657 and sheet frames 4:48.50-4:50.00 show irregular dark gaps in the upper rows of both grids after the sort.
findings.likely_cause: Each cell draws either its lit square, which moves, or its unlit square, never both. The guard on the unlit branch is dead code: `ord.indexOf(9 - floor(i/10))` is always >= 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw the unlit background square for all 100 cells first in a separate loop with no condition, then draw the lit squares on top at their lerped positions. Re-render chunk 19.

findings.frames: 9602-9628 (E11 cut and the hold after it)
findings.what_viewer_sees: The cut from the bright blue "89% water" globe to the Pacific shot drops to an unlit, nearly black globe. It stays perfectly still for about 0.8 s while the narrator says "The Pacific alone". The teal Pacific only starts to show about 0.5 s after the word "Pacific".
findings.evidence: Frame mean is 59.2 at 9600 and 6.3 at 9602, flat at 6.4 until 9625, then rises from 6.7 at 9626 to 18.2 at 9636. Frames 9598-9645 viewed.
findings.likely_cause: The Pacific highlight (pour edge sweep, with unfilled cyan alpha 150*edgeP) is keyed to tm.alone - pre (320.68) with inOut easing. The camera holds the same key until tm.drop.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the sweep to the cut and the word "Pacific", e.g. `prog(t, cPac + 0.05, tm.alone + 0.6, E.out)`, so the Pacific starts lighting up on the cut. Optionally give the first camera key a slight push (alt 2.75 to 2.6) so the shot is not frozen. Re-render chunk 21.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On "...dig to China? Argentinians.", a white outline pops on over South America at full opacity and starts flying toward China before Argentina itself is highlighted. Argentina only turns orange about 0.4 s later, after its copy has left, so cause and effect read backwards and the answer is telegraphed early.
findings.evidence: Frames 8196-8219: the outline appears at 8201 and leaves over 8205-8211; Argentina's orange fill appears over 8212-8214.
findings.likely_cause: tFlipAR0 = tm.arg - 0.6 (273.34), but the Argentina fill aa ramps from tm.arg - pre - 0.25 to tm.arg (273.59 to 273.94). The flip outline has no fade-in.
findings.suggested_fix: Light Argentina first and flip it after. For example, set aa = prog(t, tm.arg - 0.75, tm.arg - 0.45) and tFlipAR0 = tm.arg - 0.4, and fade the outline in with ctx.globalAlpha = prog(t, tFlipAR0, tFlipAR0 + 0.12) before strokeImg at line 677. Re-render chunk 18.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On "Even if you started in China", the orange China turns a washed-out grey in a single frame, then the cyan copy peels away from it.
findings.evidence: Mean RGB of a box on China goes from (144, 59, 36) at 8006 to (93, 102, 98) at 8007. Frames 7986-8032 viewed.
findings.likely_cause: The flipping copy is drawn as a 50% cyan fill plus a white stroke from the first frame after tFlipCH0. At that point ck is about 0, so the copy sits exactly on top of China with no fade-in.
findings.suggested_fix: Fade the copy in over about 0.2 s: `const ca = prog(t, tFlipCH0, tFlipCH0 + 0.2); ctx.globalAlpha = 0.5 * ca;`, and draw strokeImg at alpha ca. Alternatively, draw the copy only once ck > 0.05 so it separates from China as it appears. Re-render chunk 17.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the end card, the JUICE CHECK "?" stamp lands right on a tetra edge. A bright yellow line runs vertically through the box and through the "?", so the brand stamp looks crossed out or cluttered for the last 5 s next to SUBSCRIBE.
findings.evidence: In full-res frame 10724 a vertical edge at x of about 1300-1330 crosses the stamp and its "?" glyph. The same is visible throughout 10582-10730.
findings.likely_cause: The stamp lands at the projected globe centre (gc), and its plate is only 55% opaque, while the tetra edges are drawn additively underneath it.
findings.suggested_fix: Land the stamp clear of the projected edges (e.g. gc + (-230, 70)), or give the landed stamp an opaque plate through a bg option such as rgba(10,6,6,0.92). Re-render chunk 23.

result.intended_notes:
Intended events: E2, E3, E5, E7, E9, E11, E13, E14, E15, E16 and E17 are hard cuts on narration beats, at code cut points cBob, cAnti, cWaf, cCap, cFlip, cPac, cMont, tMont2, tMont3, tMont4 and cDrip. E14 to E16 are intended cuts, but they carry the veil bug (S4-3). E1 and the motion stops in E16 and E17 are eased ends of designed moves; E1 decays 3.25, 2.38, 1.43, 0.65, 0.16. E4 is the designed 1-in-2 to 1-in-8 counter roll. E6 is the eased 0.5 s waffle sort, which leaves holes (S4-8). E8 is a designed outExpo slide-over of the tile panel; only the black tile squares are wrong (S4-4). E10 is the designed inOutExpo 180-degree whip-flip with streaks on "globe over". E18 is the designed diagonal wipe into the 1875 scene. E12 is a real defect (S4-1 and S4-2). E19 is the known seam.

Clean stretches: the flat-map zoom to South America and the Kenney mini (no T-pose; clean rise, jump and emote). The bob gag. The antipode wipe, pulses and counter (4:36-4:45). The cap search and settle (4:50-5:07). The X-stamp slams and all pill timings, which are within about 0.1 s of their words. The flip, 89% counter and New Zealand zoom (5:12-5:20). The pour fill itself. The drip globe and cape lines. The 1875 wipe, x-ray edges (edge ends move smoothly, about 1 px per frame, no sample stepping), the flare and the camera move on "Before". The SUBSCRIBE pop.

Chunk seams 8099/8100, 8549/8550, 8999/9000, 9449/9450 and 9899/9900 show no look change, only encoder-level noise of 0.3 mean difference with no localized block and no luma shift. 10350 is the only real seam change (known).

Audio flag 5:14.85-5:15.80: the impact_deep SFX at -8 dB under "eighty-nine" sits about 7.5 dB below the voice per second (voice -14 dB, SFX -21.5 dB), and it is a low boom. I judge it acceptable; it could optionally drop to -12 dB.

Tooling warning: tools/grab.py duplicates the first frame of every multi-frame run, because ffmpeg's image2 output uses the default vsync. In its tiles, every label after the first shows the previous frame (label n is frame n-1). I verified this against raw chunk c_00021, where the E11 cut is at local 152, which is global 9602; grab.py labels it 9603. The fix is to add '-vsync', 'passthrough' to the ffmpeg call at grab.py:26. Other segment reviewers may be off by one frame. All frame numbers here come from a corrected copy at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/s4tools/grab2.py. The pack's own event strips are correctly aligned.
